recfintools

NOTE: This package is in active development. While it is ready for production use for the 2027 assessment cycle, its contents will be updated and improved, and therefore scripts using it may need to be updated

Introduction

Recreational data for stock assessments along the US West Coast have historically been obtained from a mixture of centralized and decentralized sources, using online tools or requests from individuals via email. This process required extensive coordination, and repeated back and forth between data providers and stock assessment teams to understand data fields, processing steps, and decision points, and were often repeated across species within an assessment cycle, and then again for each assessment cycle.

Efforts to standardize recreational data likely started early, but were documented and shared via github by staff at the Northwest Fisheries Science Center (NWFSC) beginning with the 2021 assessment cycle. Early versions of a package to process recreational data occurred shortly thereafter, but were not formalized into a working package until the 2027 assessment cycle.

We support the efforts of the Pacific States Marine Fisheries Commission (PSMFC) to provide a clearing house for recreational sampling data collected over the years along the US West Coast called the Recreational Fisheries Information Network (RecFIN). This package is meant to work with this data, and was developed closely with PSMFC, along with input from Washington, Oregon, and California data providers. The intended use of this package is specifically for stock assessments conducted by the NWFSC and Southwest Fisheries Science Center (SWFSC) in support of the Pacific Fishery Management Council (PFMC) process.

State Sampling Programs

Each state collects data from their recreational fisheries which is then transmitted to RecFIN:

  • CRFS: California Recreational Fisheries Survey
    • CRFS Sampling Protocol Manual
    • CRFS General Information
  • ORBS: Oregon Ocean Recreational Boats Survey
    • ORBS Sampling Design
  • OSP: Ocean Sampling Program

From 1980-2003, data collection was handled federally by the following program, with data housed in RecFIN from a legacy instance of the data.

  • MRFSS: Marine Recreational Fisheries Statistics Survey (historical)

Installation

Installing RecFIN requires the use of devtools or remotes. The latter is a dependency of the former so you can just install devtools from CRAN.

Install the most recent, stable version of the package from github using

remotes::install_github("pfmc-assessments/recfintools")

Instructions below assume that the recfintools library has been loaded using

library(recfintools)

and thus function calls are not preceded by recfintools::.

Usage

This package can be used to * Pull datasets from the RecFIN website and saves them locally * Reads saved datasets into R for processing * Filters the raw datasets and provides standardized field names

The data can then be processed and summarized for catch time series, biological relationships, and compositions for use in assessments, however the current package does not include functions that automate these processes.

Data

Reading in recreational fisheries data can be done with the pullData() and readData() functions.

pullData(path = file.path("Ling"), species = "LINGCOD")
readData(path = file.path("Ling"), species = "LINGCOD")

Generally, not all users will have access to all data reports on RecFIN so pullData() should be called by the package maintainer or recreational point of contact. To request data from this package obtained from pullData(), please create a new “Data request” issue within the github repository. Once data are provided, readData() can be used to read them into R for processing.

Cleaning data

The clean_catch() and clean_bds() functions automatically clean the data and work towards providing consistent column names such as year instead of YEAR or YR. These functions need to be called for each data set, and automatically determine the necessary fields to filter on. Consistency is key because there are so many providers of data when it comes to recreational fisheries and all use a variety of column names. Any fields added are written as lowercase column names, whereas original column names are uppercase.

These two functions call a series of sub-functions described below. While each can be called independently, it is recommended to use clean_catch or clean_bds to call these. Both clean_catch and clean_bds include an option to remove records flagged by the various sub-functions using clean = TRUE. A summary of each of the sub-functions is provided below.

#For cleaning catch data for all datasets
clean_catch()

#For cleaning biological data for each dataset.

#Use clean = FALSE to see the data sub-functions suggest should be removed.
#This option is recommended for exploring the data, but does not produce data
#ready for use within a stock assessment. For that use clean = TRUE.
bds_recent_len <- clean_bds(data = bds_recent_len, clean = FALSE, verbose = TRUE)
bds_recent_age <- clean_bds(data = bds_recent_age, clean = FALSE, verbose = TRUE)
bds_mrfss <- clean_bds(data = bds_mrfss, clean = FALSE, verbose = TRUE)

#Use clean = TRUE if you want the records suggested for removal by the
#sub-functions to be removed. This option results in data ready for inclusion
#in a stock assessment.
bds_recent_len <- clean_bds(data = bds_recent_len, clean = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)
bds_recent_age <- clean_bds(data = bds_recent_age, clean = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)
bds_mrfss <- clean_bds(data = bds_mrfss, clean = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)

State getState()

Adds a standardized column “state” that equals WA, OR, or CA. Any records without a state designation are assigned as UNK, but this is very rare. Function alerts user of the number of records without a state designation.

Year getYear()

Adds a standardized column “year”. Function alerts user of the number of records without a year designation. Additionally, notifies user that MRFSS bds records in Oregon should extend only through 2000, and ORBS bds records in Oregon should start in 2001, and prepares data beyond these bounds for removal.

Mode getMode()

Adds a standardized column “mode” that equals PR, PC, other, or unknown. Function alerts user of the number of records without a mode designation. Note that Washington historical data does not contain mode information so everything is assigned as unknown.

Mode getArea()

Notifies the user of the number of records from Canada, Puget Sound, or Mexico waters and prepares them for removal. Also notifies the user that Washington does not use MRFSS bds data, so also prepares these for removal. Additionally, this function alerts user of the number of records outside ocean areas (e.g. inland, sound, bays). Catch records in these areas are generally kept, but composition data in these areas are often removed.

Lengths getLengths()

This is used only for length bds data. Function adds a standardized column “length_cm” reported in cm. Alerts user of the number of records outside the agency determined maximum values, if lengths are reported as total lengths (and so assumes fork length as the desired measurement), or if lengths are likely not directly measured but rather derived from empirical relationships. Additionally, notifies user of any lengths that are 0 or NA, and prepares these records for removal.

Check catches check_catch()

This is used only for recent years of catch data. It notifies the user if the TOTAL_MORTALITY_MT field does not equals the sum of RELEASED_DEAD_MT and RETAINED_MT. It also checks, and notifies the user when there is catch in numbers but catch in weight is zero, implying missing weight values.

Columns cleanColumns()

This removes columns that are not commonly used from the datasets. Currently, columns consisting entirely of NA values, that have a percentage of NA values above a user specified amount (currently set to 100 percent, so for columns with all NA values), and some pre-specified columns.

Additional records removed

The clean_catch function also notifies the user that MRFSS catch records are not currently used by Washington and Oregon, and prepares these records for removal.

Processing data

There are many decision points for processing recreational data. The package currently includes only a few functions that provide default choices for processing data. It is expected that as development proceeds, the number of processing functions will expand.

Historical weights getWeightHist()

Ages getAges()
